#1949. Pressing with intensity, getting runners beyond Kane and playing like a 'Premier League team': How Thomas Tuchel's new-look England dismantled Spain - and what he's learned from cowardly retreat against Argentina

Published: 12:59 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 12:59 EST, 16 November 2026

By the end of the World Cup, it felt as if Argentina had ripped the mask off Thomas Tuchel’s England only to reveal Gareth Southgate’s England standing there blinking right back at them.

On the biggest stage, against the biggest teams, under the biggest pressure, England wilted as they always did. They sat back, they were too cautious, and they lost. And yet, ever since, Tuchel has turned England into a free-scoring winning machine, topped off by a famous victory in Madrid, ending Spain’s 43-match unbeaten streak.

In the six games since the summer, England have scored 19 goals and conceded six. Five of those have been against the world champions.

Yes, this was the Nations League and not a World Cup semi-final. No, it wasn’t at the end of a gruelling five weeks of heat, humidity and altitude. And, yes, it was only a terrific late double save from James Trafford that stopped this being yet another tale of self-sabotaging England, thanks to Elliot Anderson’s red card, blowing another lead when under pressure.

But, this time, England did see it out. They secured Tuchel’s biggest win as England boss and, in doing so, showed us just how he’s been able to get his side playing his way.

Harry Kane leads the England celebrations after his side's victory over Spain in Madrid on Sunday night

Remember when everyone used to lose their minds whenever Harry Kane dropped deep in big games under Southgate? He’s our bloody striker, for goodness sake. Get in the box!

After England’s defeat by Spain in the Euro 2024 final two years ago, Opta posted on X that Kane had touched the ball just once in the opposition box across both that game and their previous final heartbreak against Italy three years earlier.

‘One fewer than Jack Grealish,’ the post continued. ‘Grealish played 21 minutes in the 2020 final and didn't make the Euro 2024 squad.’

Ballon d’Or winner Kane has made it quite clear since that he doesn’t need to spend all his time in the box to influence games. When he drops deeper, Kane is able to show the full extent of his creativity and range of passing.

The main problem with the ploy under Southgate, however, was that Kane rarely had the team-mates to make the right runs ahead of him. He was surrounded by players who wanted to take up similar positions. Just look at the average position maps (below) from England’s loss to Spain at Euro 2024 compared to last night.

The average position map of England’s players in the loss to Spain at Euro 2024 show how Kane dropped deep, without team-mates making runs for him to exploit

...whereas on Sunday night he had runners - Anthony Gordon, Jude Bellingham and Morgan Rogers - around and beyond him

Two years ago, the only player who averaged their touches ahead of Kane was Bukayo Saka. Jude Bellingham was out wide. Kobbie Mainoo and Phil Foden were basically in Kane’s shadow.

On Sunday night, he had Anthony Gordon, the brilliant, belligerent Bellingham and Morgan Rogers all ahead of him – and nearly even Ben White.

That desire, and instruction, to flock forward under Tuchel has made such a difference.

Take England’s third goal (below). Kane has the ball outside the area. Rogers is bombing on to his left. Gordon, who started as a winger but finds himself occupying the central spaces Kane leaves behind, darts into the box and points to where he wants it.

Bellingham is demanding the ball, too, showing Kane he wants it to feet. Even Anderson is charging into the box. Kane finds Bellingham, who feeds the unseen White, sprinting forward on the overlap to finish.

Kane picks up the ball and is met with an array of options in front of him, ahead of England's third goal

He did similar in the win against Croatia a few days earlier, too.

Kane collects the ball deep with four bodies ahead of him, including full backs Lewis Hall and Trent Alexander-Arnold.

It his raking pass to the back post which allows Bellingham to set up Rogers to finish.

Kane's lofted pass to Rogers (top right) leads to a goal against Croatia for Bellingham (edge of box)

England’s fluidity in the final third is bamboozling defences. That is how you get the best of Kane’s creativity.

Football is changing, so Pep Guardiola told us all in January last year. The modern game is now how teams like Bournemouth and Brighton play. The current Premier League table would suggest he had a point.

Over the past few years in the English top flight, we have seen teams move away from an obsession with keeping the ball for the sake of it and turn towards a far faster, more aggressive and more physical style of play.

Tuchel wants to take from that playbook. ‘We're at our best when we're free, physically overpowering and making it Premier League-level,’ said Kane after last month's 7-0 rout of Croatia.

In the six matches since the World Cup, Tuchel’s England are having much less of the ball than they did at the start of his reign – and now less even than under Southgate.

The key is they are becoming ever more direct with it. Tuchel wants his England to play out of the back with short passes, entice opponents on to them, but then move it through the lines at speed.

Since the World Cup, England are playing far fewer passes, but more of them into the box – to find those runners. A higher percentage of them forward. More direct attacks, moving the ball up the field at a quicker speed.

On Sunday night, they showed how Tuchel wants his side to press. ‘We were hungry in the opposition half,’ said the England boss at full time.

A fine example of that (below) came just after just six minutes. Declan Rice gives his Arsenal team-mate Martín Zubimendi no time at all on the ball inside his own area, charging him down, and forcing him to play out to another Gunner in Mikel Merino. But he, too, is being harassed by Anderson and eventually England win it back and set up Kane for a chance that he fizzes wide.

A half-fit Rice was unable to apply that pressure in the summer.

Declan Rice charges forward to close down Martin Zubimendi who has possession just inside the Spanish box with Kane and Bellingham already engaged in a high press...

...Zubimendi passes to Mikel Merino but Elliot Anderson is all over him and it leads to Kane shot that just fizzes wide

So much of this improvement under Tuchel into a side capable of blowing teams away can be put down to another abstract word he used post-match in Madrid: ‘brave’.

Tuchel talked in the last international break of ‘unlocking the next level’, and taking ‘calculated risks’ with a ‘man-to-man’ press in the opposition half.

Under Southgate, and certainly in the cowardly retreat against Argentina in the summer, England showed little bravery either with the ball or without it and frequently showed too much respect to those big nations.

Too safe with the ball, too afraid to give it away, and too fearful to try to win it back in case you leave yourself open.

That appears to be changing, too. There was a moment at the start of the second half when Bellingham tried a risky through-ball to Rogers, which failed to find its man, instead of another simple ball out wide.

It handed Spain possession cheaply. But England didn’t care because they just pounced again. Spain couldn’t deal with it. In the first half, Spain completed just 84 per cent of their passes in their own half – a place where they are usually able to knock it about at will – their lowest completion rate according to Opta since the 2010 World Cup. They didn’t have a shot on target until the penalty.

England’s defence has long been seen as the weak spot and, under Southgate, it felt as though he always would rather his attacking talents not be too frivolous for fear of exposing it.

Thomas Tuchel and Kane direct England's players to keep on the front foot during the win over Spain

Tuchel is doing the opposite. England’s expected goals soared from 1.7 per game under Southgate from the 2022 World Cup to the end of his reign, to 2.2 under Tuchel’s until this summer’s tournament. Since then, it’s jumped again to 2.8 but at the cost of what they are conceding. In his early days, England coughed up fewer good chances than under Southgate but since the World Cup has more than doubled.

He will want to get that down, of course, but when you are creating so much – and have an array of top finishers to see them off – how much will that matter to Tuchel?

Even he’s getting braver. His decision to take off Gordon for Konsa and chuck as many defenders on during England’s shrinking against Argentina looked a decision that would forever haunt Tuchel’s tenure.

Against Spain, Kane made way but Tuchel ended the game with striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin on the pitch. Against Spain, he held his nerve.

#1948. Late winner at Selsey keeps Worthing United’s promotion bid firing

The Mavericks once again demonstrated the character, resilience and never-say-die attitude that have become hallmarks of their recent performances, snatching all three points in dramatic fashion.

The result followed an impressive 2-0 win at Saltdean United and moved Worthing United up to third place, with 36 points from 17 matches.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Under joint managers Glenn Souter and Mark Curram, United have now collected 17 points from their last possible 21, recording five victories and two draws.

That sequence has included victories over Guildford City, Shoreham, Arundel, Saltdean and Selsey, alongside hard-fought draws against league leaders Infinity and promotion rivals Jarvis Brook.

It has been a run that has tested the Mavericks in different ways. From the dramatic late equaliser against Infinity to recovering from two goals down at Jarvis Brook, the side have shown a growing belief that they can get a result regardless of the circumstances.

Souter commented: “Saturday probably summed up where we are as a group at the moment. We weren’t necessarily at our best, but the players kept believing right until the final whistle, and to get a winner so late on was a fantastic feeling.

“Looking back over the last seven league matches, I’m really pleased with what the lads have produced. We’ve played some very good football, but equally importantly, we’ve shown the other side of our game. We’ve had to dig deep, defend properly, come from behind and find ways to win.

“That’s what successful teams have to do. You aren’t going to dominate every game over a long season, particularly in this league, but you have to be prepared to fight for every point.

“We’ve got a really good group of lads here who are playing for each other. The togetherness in the dressing room is excellent, and even when things aren’t going our way, there’s a genuine belief that we can turn games around.

“Seventeen points from 21 is a fantastic return, but we’re not getting carried away. We know there are areas where we can improve, and I still believe there’s another level in this team.

“After coming so close last season, the lads know what’s required. We’re determined to keep pushing, stay amongst the leading sides and give ourselves the best possible chance of achieving something special this season.

“The coaches, Craig Nagle and Jack Willis have been brilliant, and hopefully we can keep giving them a platform to grow and develop the team alongside us. There’s a long way to go, but the spirit and determination we’re showing at the moment are exactly what we need.”

With the Mavericks firmly in the promotion picture, their recent form and remarkable fighting spirit are providing plenty of reasons for optimism at Lyons Way.

They host struggling Dorking Wanderers B on Saturday.

#1947. Tuttosport: Not just Endrick and Tresoldi – Milan eyeing Bundesliga striker Krösche admires

A new idea has emerged for AC Milan to strengthen their attack, and it is a player that incoming Head of Football Markus Krösche knows well.

This morning’s edition of Tuttosport writes that the two dreams for January are Nicolò Tresoldi and Endrick, but a third option is starting to emerge at Milan. The player is equally effective in terms of goals, but perhaps less media-burdened than Gonçalo Ramos.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The Portuguese striker has just three goals so far for Milan since joining for a club-record €73m fee, and his current drought is now over one month. This is why finding a viable alternative in the winter is key, but perhaps without spending another €60-70m on another forward.

It will be very hard to snatch Tresoldi from Club Brugge during the winter transfer window, as Arsenal and Atletico Madrid are also strongly interested in him. Meanwhile, Endrick’s departure from Real Madrid is currently being vetoed by Jose Mourinho. So, who could the Rossoneri turn to?

Milan could look towards the Bundesliga, more specifically Stuttgart’s Ermedin Demirovic. He is a name highly regarded by Milan’s new Head of Football – Markus Krösche – who has watched him up close for several years.

The Bosnian striker’s contract expires in 2028, and there’s currently no agreement to extend it. Therefore, his price tag – despite an  excellent start to the season – isn’t likely to skyrocket and could become affordable.

He’s already scored nine goals across all competitions: five in nine appearances in the league, and four in four in the Champions League. That seems to provide enough evidence that the Bosnia international is ready for a top club.

Ermedin Demirovic has scored a hat-trick in the first 32 minutes of Stuttgart's game with Viking.

It's the fifth earliest in Champions League history:

🇵🇱 Robert Lewandowski vs. RB Salzburg (23rd minute)🇮🇹 Marco Simone vs. Rosenborg (24th minute)🇫🇷 Kylian Mbappe vs.… pic.twitter.com/V5XA1iEwLg

— The Athletic | Football (@TheAthleticFC) September 9, 2026

Demirovic is raring to go and is eyeing potential suitors (including several English clubs). A couple of years ago, Juventus sought him as a partner to Dusan Vlahovic , when Cristiano Giuntoli was still in charge. Now, that move to Italy might finally come about.

In recent weeks, the presence of Milan scouts at Stuttgart’s matches has not gone unnoticed. Demirovic has responded in his own way: with goals. Dzeko’s heir in the Bosnian national team can also play as a second striker and therefore, if necessary, partner Ramos.

In the past he has also been used as a winger in a three-man attack. This versatility is invaluable for a chameleon-like coach like Ruben Amorim, and it would allow Ermedin to be used in any type of situation.

It would also facilitate Francesco Camarda’s possible loan exit, so this is a situation well worth watching as we reach the weeks leading up to the winter window.

#1945. Omar Berrada hits back at criticism over Manchester United’s transfer strategy

Manchester United’s CEO Omar Berrada has hit back at criticism of the club’s transfer strategy last summer and insists a ‘disciplined’ approach is required.

United spent £155 million on signing three midfielders in Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba in the summer transfer window.

However, Mauricio Pochettino arrives at Old Trafford this week without a recognised striker as Benjamin Sesko is out for the remainder of the year with a shin problem, while Luke Shaw has missed United’s last seven games due to injury.

United supporters have criticised the club’s decision to only strengthen Michael Carrick’s midfield in the summer but Berrada is adamant the squad is ‘fundamentally better’ after their signings.

‘You have to take it in the context of the last few years,’ Berrada told Sky Sports.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

‘The summer of 2025, I think the recruitment team was widely praised with the four players that were signed. And they did very well. They helped the team achieve Champions League qualification.

‘When we look at this summer, we went in knowing what we needed to do. Of course, there have been different dynamics at play. It’s probably been the summer or the transfer window where there’s been the highest inflation in transfer fees.

‘And we’ve said publicly and we’ve said consistently in the last few years that we need to stay disciplined. We need to take the right decisions. We need to buy the right players for the right value at the right time in terms of what the squad needs.

‘And when we look at the summer transfer window of 2026, I know we’re receiving a lot of criticism for it but we’re actually happy with the players that we bought.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘We think that Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Karl Darlow, and let’s not forget that we’ve also welcomed back Marcus Rashford, who had a very good season on loan at Barcelona – these are five additions that we think have made the squad fundamentally better.

‘It’s true that we lost Casemiro, who is a top player and gave a lot to the club. We also lost Manuel Ugarte to, unfortunately, an ACL injury. So our focus was very much about straightening the midfield.

‘When we started the transfer window, we really only had Kobbie Mainoo as our midfielder. So we wanted to reinforce that, and we did it.’

Berrada also addressed United’s decision not to sign a new left-sided defender after the club made an enquiry for Newcastle United’s Lewis Hall in the summer.

‘When you look at the other areas of the pitch, and there’s a lot of discussion about the back line,’ Berrada said.

‘But we did come into it thinking we have depth. We have nine players that can play in the back line, in the back four positions.

‘So that’s why we looked primarily at investing in the midfield. But we were always looking for opportunities. I think it’s been widely reported that we were looking at potentially the left-back position as a reinforcement.

‘I think what we’ve seen in the back line is we’ve had injuries, it’s taken Matthijs de Ligt longer than we would want it to get back. Unfortunately, Luke Shaw suffered a muscle injury that meant he was out for five or six weeks.

‘So could we have signed an additional defender to straighten the depth and the quality? Yes, but we have to find the right players and you have to find the right players at the right value.

‘There’s no point in us spending £40 million, £50m for players that we’re not convinced are going to add value to the team.

‘So it’s always about being disciplined and finding the right opportunities and getting the right players that are going to take us forward.

‘When I talk about being disciplined, I talk about not overspending on players that don’t necessarily add quality to the team.

‘Because when you sign a player that doesn’t work out for Man Utd, it becomes very difficult to move that player on or to get the sale we want. And that can set us back.

‘So when I talk about being disciplined, I’m not talking about necessarily not spending to get the top players. We have the ambition to win, to win the Premier League, to win the Champions League, to win the domestic cups. And for that, we need top talent. So when we find the right opportunities, we will spend. But what we don’t want to be doing is spending just for the sake of it.’

#1944. Young guns down Harrogate to give Worthing a statement National League win

After levelling matters in first-half stoppage-time, Young popped up three minutes from time to sweep home Cory Adjetey-Brew’s searching low delivery to complete a comeback over the Sulphurites.

There was space in the starting XI for both Dominic Johnson-Fisher and Queens Park Rangers loanee Emmerson Sutton, with Sam Clucas on the bench on his first Woodside matchday.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

The first 20 minutes were edged by the hosts, but they were unable to convert pressure into an opening goal. Several crosses and corners were defended astutely by Harrogate, with a deflected delivery from the right side volleyed wide from close-range by Sutton.

As a result of the positioning and press from the visiting side, the Rebels backline were limited to sending direct long balls over the top to look for the pacy Johnson-Fisher. One clearance forward was pounced upon by the former Truro City man, whose mishit effort still forced keeper Luke Hutchinson to push behind for a corner.

However, disaster struck midway through the first period as a rash defensive decision proved costly. Following Hutchinson’s clever distribution with a quickly-taken throw, Joe Cook galloped across on a quest to intercept, only to be beaten to it by Ciaran McGuckin.

With the defender taken out of the game, McGuckin proceeded to feed the darting run of Will McGowan and his finish rifled into the roof of the net to put the Yorkshire-based outfit in front against the run of play.

The Reds looked vulnerable. Sensing this frailty, Simon Weaver’s side probed and captain Lewis Cass’ effort was repelled by Harrison Foulkes into McGowan’s path, with the scorer connecting wildly on the rebound on the half-volley.

Just shy of the half-hour, the upright came to Worthing’s rescue. A heavy touch from Cook drew in the attention of Shawn McCoulsky and McGuckin latched on to the loose ball with his teammate brought down by the recovering defender. Opting to strike early, the side-footed attempt from Harrogate’s No35 caught out Foulkes before bouncing off the post – and Cook made amends on the rebound.

The Reds reclaimed some control and searched for parity. Razzaq Coleman De-Graft fashioned an opportunity to shoot with persistent footwork, but Hutchinson gathered the attempt prior to Sutton’s shot from close quarters being smothered.

But perseverance paid off just before the interval as Young found a way through a retreating Harrogate defence. Digging out a cross into a congested area, neither Ricky Aguiar nor Johnson-Fisher could apply a touch, which deceived Hutchinson and allowed the ball to travel all the way through and into the back of the net – and that was Young slightly fortuitous fifth goal of the season.

That offered the hosts a blank slate heading into the second period and they built on that foundation in the opening exchanges with Sutton providing enthusiasm down the left flank. An inventive free-kick from Young scooped possession in Coleman De-Graft’s direction, but his subsequent volley was blazed over.

The encounter devolved into a tense and fragmented one but as the match opened up, Ellis Taylor’s drive was thwarted by Foulkes before the goalkeeper had to backtrack at breakneck speed to prevent Jayden Moore’s backpass from going in.

With the clock ticking towards 90, the Reds were in the ascendancy as they seemed more likely to find a winner. And found it ewas in minute 87 after a flowing team move.

Johnson-Fisher’s slide-rule pass slipped in Adjetey-Brew, who did superbly on the stretch to fire into the middle. Falling into Young’s path, the man of the moment coolly slotted into the bottom corner to send Woodside into raptures.

The closing stages were met with maturity and composure from Adam Hinshelwood’s team as they sealed their first league win of the month over a play-off rival.

#1943. Steyning Town’s fightback falls short in defeat to Punjab United

The floodlights came on just ten minutes into a cold Saturday afternoon, and a crowd of 125 saw Punjab race into a four-goal lead inside 34 minutes. Steyning pulled two back after the break, but the visitors held on for a 4–2 win.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Punjab took the lead with the first chance of the game. Emmanuel Oluwasemo picked out Chris Edwards at the back post with a fine delivery, and Edwards headed in off the post.

A couple of minutes later, Edwards turned provider, picking out Roman Campbell, whose bullet header flew past Alfie Mansell to make it 2–0.

Things went from bad to worse for the Barrowmen before the half-hour. Campbell pounced on a mistake by Marcus Allen and squared for Jack Hopkins, who rolled the ball into an empty net for Punjab’s third.

Steyning were forced into a change when Max Blencowe went off injured after a late studs-up tackle. The Punjab defender was shown a yellow card, while some thought the challenge worthy of a red. Bright Kuntu-Blankson came on to replace Blencowe.

Midway through the half, Jesse Sentamu came off the bench to score for the second week running, pulling one back with his third goal of the season.

Steyning kept up the pressure and Jared Rance added a second in the 90th minute. But The first-half damage proved too much to undo, and Punjab left the Shooting Field with all three points.

Punjab’s win extended their unbeaten league run to eight matches and lifted them to ninth in the table while the Barrowmen dropped to 15th.

#1941. OLIVER HOLT: Why England CAN now end 62 years of hurt - Thomas Tuchel is intoxicating and I'd tip Jude Bellingham to beat Kylian Mbappe to the next Ballon d'Or... plus my top 10 Three Lions performances

Published: 12:00 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 13:04 EST, 16 November 2026

The glum face of Lamine Yamal, head in hands, stared out from the front page of the Spanish sports paper AS as it sat on newspaper stands in Madrid on Monday morning. ‘Fin a la racha,’ the headline said. The end of the run.

For Spain football fans, England’s 3-2 dramatic victory over the world champions in the Spanish capital on Sunday evening made this akin to a day of mourning, the first time their team had tasted defeat in 44 matches, an end to a gilded period of invincibility.

For England, the feeling was very different. Because Sunday night in the cauldron of the Metropolitano felt very much like a beginning. Thomas Tuchel has been the head coach for almost two years but this was the moment of his true arrival.

This was the victory that freed us from looking back to the Groundhog Day pain of that World Cup semi-final defeat by Argentina in Atlanta last summer and allowed us to look forward to a future that seems luminous and full of hope.

This was the victory that allowed us to stop blaming Tuchel for what happened four months ago and start looking forwards again, dreaming about the glories that he might yet deliver. This was the victory that validated Tuchel and why the FA hired him in the first place. This was the victory that allowed us to believe he might be the Messiah after all.

This felt like the moment when he embraced us, with all our quirks and football idiosyncrasies, and we embraced him. He had promised ‘proof of concept’ on the eve of the game and he delivered it with bells on. Tuchel has harnessed the best of the English game and welded it to his principles and the result is intoxicating.

Thomas Tuchel has harnessed the best of the English game to down world champions Spain

Once you have seen England play the way they did for an hour against Spain, you are lost. You are lost to the belief that the 62 years of hurt might really be coming to an end at Wembley in the final of the European Championship in the summer of 2028. You are lost to the idea that, finally, everything is falling into place.

For the 63 minutes up until the sending off of Elliot Anderson, I have never seen an England performance as good as the one that unfolded in the Metropolitano. Spain are the best team in the world and England outclassed them and stupefied them. They were better than them with the ball and better than them without the ball. They were magnificent.

Because of the context, because of the wonder of the stage, because of the odds they faced, England’s victory over Mexico in the grandeur and the mayhem of the mighty Azteca Stadium during the World Cup might edge Sunday’s performance but for pure football, what England delivered in Madrid demands comparison with the best they have played for many a year.

This year’s World Cup came just too soon but now Tuchel and England understand each other perfectly. And now England are purring. They have a manager who commands the players’ respect and they have a group of players that commands the respect of the manager.

Yes, it was just a Nations League group game but it was against one of the best national sides the world has ever seen. England worked so ferociously and attacked so fluently and defended so devotedly that they reached a level that drew admiration even from their opponents.

Many, many things will live long in the memory. James Trafford’s miraculous double save in the dying minutes gets better every time I watch it. Ben White’s goal channels the beauty of Carlos Alberto’s strike for Brazil against Italy in the 1970 World Cup Final, too. Let’s hope that strike, and his superb defensive performance, bring an end to the boos that have been his companion of late.

Jude Bellingham was relentless, tireless and glided through the game against Spain

Tuchel had promised ‘proof of concept’ on the eve of the game and he delivered it

And then there was Jude Bellingham. Just when you think you can’t admire him any more than you do, he delivers a performance like the one he produced against Spain, a performance that lifted him above even the exalted company of the other players on two fine teams.

Bellingham was tireless. He was relentless. He glided past challenges. He thundered into tackles. He dominated midfield. He has the heart and the sheer brilliant indomitability that Bryan Robson possessed.

Bellingham has it in him to be England’s greatest ever player. He needs trophies to fulfil that destiny but maybe, finally, trophies are in reach again.

He has the team around him to do it, which Robson never quite had. Jordan Pickford is a good goalkeeper but Trafford might just be better. Ezri Konsa had his best game for England in Spain. White and Lewis Hall were superb at full back. Little more needs to be said about England’s front six. They are as good as any unit in world football.

Harry Kane, of course, was the best player in the world last year. Some seem to assume that the Ballon d’Or will inevitably pass to Yamal or Kylian Mbappe next. I think it is more likely to be Bellingham.

The man is a colossus. He is a footballer who has everything. He does not know how to be beaten.

Bellingham saw off Barcelona rival Lamine Yamal - and could beat him to the Ballon d'Or

With them together, the sky is the limit. And Bellingham has also proved to be a player of immense mental strength. It was not so long ago that people worried about his discipline but the fortitude he showed when he was being targeted by Argentina at the World Cup was the best answer to that.

He and Kane are England’s axis of ambition on the pitch. Tuchel is lucky to have them and they are lucky to have him, too. The coach has reached the point where his tactics and his team-building are bearing fruit.

Now England have a team-manager package that genuinely need fear nobody. The victory against Spain was a rehearsal for the bigger stage of major tournaments. Going down to 10 men after 63 minutes against the best team in the world might not have been in the script but that is what rehearsals are for.

After Sunday night in the Metropolitano, England are ready for their close-up.

#1940. ‘Standards needed to be raised' – New Crawley Town defender gives 'brutally honest' assessment following Fleetwood win

Experienced Heneghan came straight into Kevin Blackwell’s starting XI in the 2-1 win against Fleetwood Town on Saturday (November 21), playing as one of three centre-backs in a 3-5-2 formation.

And he repaid the new permanent manager’s faith with a dominant aerial display.

Following the game, Heneghan said: “Standards needed to be raised, I’ll be brutally honest, and as time goes on we’ll get those standards better and better.

“We’ve just got to keep working and sticking together. It’s a good group and the more we play together we’ll win some points.”

The 33 year-old’s performance was an example of driving the Reds’ standards forward from the back.

He won more than his fair share of headers and set the tone inside the first 10 minutes with a sliding block to stop a fierce Fleetwood strike from range in their first effort on goal.

Speaking about the importance of breaking their Broadfield Stadium hoodoo and earning a crucial first three points at home in the league, Heneghan said: “For the group it’s great, obviously they [Crawley] won against Oldham as well so it’s back-to-back wins in the league, which is great for confidence and morale and building on that really.”

Reflecting on his first league match in six months, the former Fleetwood player added: “Personally, it’s massive just to be back out there playing football and the relief of getting three points, so we’ve got to build on that.

“It’s the best, it’s all I’ve known since I started playing at the age of four. So, I want to continue for as long as possible until the body doesn’t work.”

Blackwell’s Reds remain unbeaten in his opening three games since taking over the reigns and singled out the performances of Heneghan, Pemi Aderoju and Danilo Orsi in Town’s first league victory since March this year.

Speaking in the post-match press conference, Blackwell said: “I thought Ben Heneghan came in, his first game for six months – I thought he did terrific. I thought [it was] maybe Pemi’s (Aderoju) best game since I’ve been here.

“[Danilo] Orsi – he’s worked so hard in training and I thought, today, he covered every blade of ground. I thought they all did well. It looked a very good unit today.

“But I want more. I need more, from certain aspects of the game and we’re hopefully trying to develop that now.”

Heneghan is only focused on the Reds’ future performances on the pitch and made it clear that the squad understands the manager’s individual and collective expectations.

He said: “What’s happened has happened and it’s gone now. The manager’s committed until the end of the season so that’s reassuring for everyone. Everyone knows their role and everyone knows what part they’re going to play.”

Crawley welcome second-placed Barnet to Broadfield on Tuesday night (November 24) and have the chance to climb out of the relegation zone with another win.

#1939. GdS: A red-hot start and the ‘S’ word – the data that inspires confidence in Amorim

A statistic has been doing the rounds regarding Ruben Amorim’s league record with AC Milan, which is gathering some attention.

His style of play is open to criticism, his selections are controversial, his words are regularly quite strong and he’s often called into question at the first sign of failure. For Amorim, his first months with the Rossoneri have been a rollercoaster ride.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

There have been ups and downs: things have been better domestically, culminating in a derby victory over Inter, but in the Europa League the one win from four games means the Rossoneri currently sit outside the playoff zone.

As La Gazzetta dello Sport write, there is a key bit of data to contextualise things. With 24 points in his first 11 Serie A matches, Amorim is averaging 2.18 points per game, the result of seven wins, three draws, and one defeat.

It is the highest ever for a Milan coach in the three-point era, ahead of Stefano Pioli, Carlo Ancelotti and Massimiliano Allegri. Looking at coaches with at least five stints in the Italian top flight, only Antonio Conte boasts a better figure than the Portuguese coach, with 2.21 points per game.

This is obviously an unfair comparison, given that the former Napoli coach’s points average takes into account all 279 of his Serie A games – with spells at Atalanta, Juventus, Inter and Napoli – compared to just 11 for the former United manager.

However, it is a testament to the excellent work done thus far by Amorim and his staff. Even more so in a season in which the decision was made to undertake a revolution in several respects, to relaunch a team and a fan base that had been burned by the collapse of last season.

Gerry Cardinale and the ownership made significant investments during the last transfer window, spending €70m on Goncalo Ramos and €50m on Diego Moreira, plus €25m on Mario Gila. This is also why Milan fans have high expectations for Amorim’s era.

To date, the average from these first 11 games project the Rossoneri to land around 83 points by the end of the season. Last year, Inter won the Scudetto with 87 points, and 71 were needed to finish fourth, the minimum target set by the owners.

Allegri’s Milan stopped at 70 points, despite a strong start to the season that even fuelled a few Scudetto dreams for a few months. That start, however, was inferior to this season: a year ago, after 11 matchdays, AC Milan had 22 points, two fewer than under Amorim.

It is an encouraging beginning to the new era that fans hope will translate into concrete results, perhaps even the Scudetto, a target announced by owner Cardinale as a real aim, as unrealistic as it may have seemed before a ball was kicked.

Amorim is trying to convey his vision of football and instil a more European mentality in his team, and the numbers so far – at least in the league – seem to prove him right. To find a better start to a season one must rewind to 2022-23, when Milan had 26 points from 11 games under Pioli.

Ruben Amorim has the highest points-per-game average of any #ACMilan coach in Serie A in the three-points-per-win era: 2.18 over 11 matches.

Among all coaches with 5+ stints in the league during that period, only Antonio Conte (2.21) has a higher average.

[via @OptaPaolo] pic.twitter.com/jwPLgVw0z7

— MilanData📊 (@acmilandata) November 19, 2026

Speaking of Pioli, in the specific ranking of Milan coaches with the highest points average – led by Amorim, as mentioned – the coach who led the Rossoneri to their 19th Scudetto (2021-22) occupies second place at 2.02 points per game in 183 Serie A matches.

Pioli also achieved the best start in Milan’s history: in the Scudetto year, he earned 31 points from the opening 11 games, the result of 10 wins and 1 draw, with a record average of 2.82 points per game.

In third place among Milan coaches with the highest points average is Ancelotti, with 1.95 points in 283 Serie A games as Milan coach. Allegri is just off the podium, with 1.91 points in 172 games across his two spells at the club.

To compare Amorim with two of his compatriots who recently worked at Milanello, Paulo Fonseca averaged just 1.59 points per game from 17 games, while Sergio Conceicao fared slightly better with 1.71 points in 21 games.

In short, Amorim’s performance is encouraging, but still relative given the very limited sample size. A crucial month is now beginning for Milan: a seven-game tour de force before Christmas that will reveal a lot about the true ambitions of the coach and his team, with form in Europe to fix.

#1938. Antonio Conte sends message to Man Utd after missing out on Mauricio Pochettino’s job

Antonio Conte has played down suggestions he missed out on the Manchester United job because of his demanding reputation in management.

United made their third mid-season managerial change in three years after sacking Michael Carrick with Mauricio Pochettino coming in as his replacement earlier this month.

Conte was among the names initially explored along with Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann. The Italian, a free agent since parting ways with Napoli, was thought to be keen on the role at Old Trafford but it was widely reported United had reservations over some of his methods.

The Italian led Juventus, Chelsea, Inter Milan and Napoli to league titles but has not lasted longer than two seasons at any club since leaving the Bianconeri in 2014.

Conte has a reputation for being hugely demanding with players and the board but in an interview with Cronache di Spogliatoio he insisted anyone scared of his approach is scared of winning.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

The coach recalled a meeting with Sir Alex Ferguson during his time in charge of Chelsea, praising the standards the Scot said before insisting the idea United no longer want to meet those standards is ‘offensive’

‘If someone is scared of my method, then they’re scared of winning, because that methodology leads to winning,’ Conte said.

Harry Kane is facing several months out after suffering an ankle ligament injury during Bayern Munich’s Bundesliga game on Friday night.

#1934. Hull City hero reveals unusual good-luck charm after dramatic win over 'excellent' Brighton

The Tigers scored twice in stoppage time at the MKM Stadium on Sunday (November 22) to secure their first win since August, with McBurnie netting in the 92nd and 95th minutes.

But while McBurnie grabbed the headlines with his late double, Hull's victory owed much to an outstanding performance from Tzolakis, who kept Brighton at bay during a difficult first half.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Jakirovic admitted his side had been made to suffer before the break, with the goalkeeper producing several important saves.

Speaking to Sky Sports, he said: "We played against an excellent team today, very high intensity. In the first half we survived and Konstantinos Tzolakis saved us four or five times.

"We had more stability in the second half. We won 2-0 and I'm extremely happy because we wait almost three months [for another win] which is unbelievable.

"Congratulations to my boys because it was not an easy game but in the end we won."

Jakirovic also felt his side had taken advantage of the opportunity presented by Costinha's 89th-minute dismissal.

"The second yellow card I think there is no problem about that and we used that moment," he said.

McBurnie was quick to acknowledge the contribution of his goalkeeper, admitting Hull had ridden their luck against a Brighton side he described as a top team.

Speaking to Sky Sports, he said: "We haven't lost a game at home. They are a top team and we knew it was going to be tough.

"We rode our luck and we have the big man [Tzolakis] to keep the ball out of the net so that's what he's done."

The striker also revealed the unusual good-luck charm he had taken onto the pitch – a toy rabbit belonging to his daughter.

"My daughter when I leave for work every game she makes me take something with me for good luck," he explained.

"Today it was her bun bun because that's what she had in her hand. It's all good fun and I'm sure she will be happy with that one."

McBurnie was equally full of praise for Tzolakis, jokingly referring to him as 'the cat' when speaking to Match of the Day.

"It's his job. That's what he's there for. The cat was brilliant today and we are lucky to have him," he said.

"Brighton are a top team and we knew we were going to be suffering and ride our luck at times, but with a bit of luck and with the cat in net we rode our luck and stayed in the game."

'The football for the goals was brilliant'

McBurnie also reflected on the importance of ending Hull's wait for a victory, although he insisted it had not felt like such a long time because of the team's strong home form.

"Buzzing for the boys because we haven't won for a while," he said.

"It doesn't feel like that because our home run has been really good. To get that three points today was massive."

The Scottish striker was particularly pleased with the way Hull worked the ball for both goals.

Regan Slater and Lucas Gourna-Douath combined to set him up for the opener before Mohamed Belloumi created the second with a run and pass across goal.

"You love those ones, especially the second one when you are passing it into an empty net. It's a lovely feeling," he said.

"If you look at the actual football for the goals it was brilliant football."

The manager also praised Tzolakis again in his BBC Match of the Day interview, describing his performance as ‘unbelievable’ and highlighting the importance of the clean sheet.

#1933. Thomas Frank announced as Crystal Palace boss as he eyes raid on Chelsea set-piece guru marginalised under Xabi Alonso

By BOBBY MANZI, FOOTBALL REPORTER and KIERAN GILL, MAIL SPORT REPORTER

Published: 10:07 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 13:08 EST, 16 November 2026

Thomas Frank has been unveiled as Crystal Palace’s new manager on a two-and-a-half-year deal.

Frank has been out of work since being sacked by Tottenham Hotspur in February and has taken a significant pay cut to take over at Palace, who languish at the bottom of the Premier League.

However, he will earn more than his predecessor, Pierre Sage, who was sacked last week after winning just two of his ten league matches in charge.

New Palace boss Frank said: ‘It's an honour to sit here and be in charge of this fantastic Football Club. I'm really, really looking forward to it.

‘Crystal Palace is an iconic club in England and in the Premier League. I will do everything I possibly can to help and support the players and everyone around the place, and I'm really looking forward to meeting them.’

Across his spells at Brentford and Tottenham, Frank has managed 178 Premier League matches with a 34 per cent win rate.

Palace are set to approach Chelsea about Bernardo Cueva, who worked with Frank at Brentford before being poached to become the Blues' set-piece specialist.

We are pleased to confirm the appointment of Thomas Frank as Manager 🤝ℹ️ https://t.co/2wUzZAGt4S pic.twitter.com/zv2vMPGPFz

Palace are set to approach Chelsea about Cueva (right), who worked with Frank at Brentford

But Cueva may now be elevated back to the forefront of football if Palace can strike an agreement to bring him in to join Frank’s backroom staff. It is said Chelsea paid Brentford around £1million in compensation to hire him in 2024 at a time when his stock was high.

Cueva arrived at Chelsea in 2024. However, Daily Mail Sport revealed in the last summer how the 39-year-old Mexican’s role was changing after two seasons of work as Xabi Alonso’s side hired Austin MacPhee from Aston Villa as their new lead on set-plays.

Cueva has not been seen since then, either in training at Cobham or at matches at Stamford Bridge, but continued to work for Chelsea in more of an analytical role behind the scenes.

Club sources stressed at the time that it should not be seen as a demotion, and he is still listed on the first-team staff section of the website under the title ‘technical analyst’.

Chelsea are due to play Palace in two weeks' time at the Bridge on Wednesday, December 2.

Chelsea previously identified Cueva as a prime candidate for a role which had been vacant since Anthony Barry exited for Bayern Munich. Cueva, who also holds a UEFA Pro Licence through the Football Association, was regarded as an impressive acquisition in 2024.

Before joining Brentford in 2020 and helping them secure promotion to the Premier League, Cueva was at Chivas in his homeland of Mexico. He has also had a role with Norway men's national team.

#1931. Three Bridges show signs of life with much-needed win against Cheshunt

Following a more encouraging performance against Dartford on Tuesday evening, Bridges knew that nothing less than three points would do if they were to stand any chance of remaining a Step 3 side next season. And it was the home side who started on the front foot, dominating much of the first half and creating a number of opportunities. Noel Leighton, Reece Hallard, Hayden Velvick and Charlie Bennett all went close inside the opening 25 minutes, but none could find a way past Cheshunt goalkeeper Rex Porter.

Against the run of play, however, the visitors took the lead. Hayden Neathey conceded a needless free-kick just outside the penalty area, and Joe Re stepped up to curl the ball past Sam Roberts. That familiar sinking feeling descended over Jubilee Field, and despite having enjoyed the better of the half, Bridges went into the interval a goal behind.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

But this time, there was no heads dropping. Bridges continued where they had left off, and their positive approach was eventually rewarded.

After seeing an attempted lob saved by Porter, Leighton and his teammates finally found a way through, with the lively Hayden Velvick restoring parity. Picking up the ball on the right-hand side of the penalty area, the winger unleashed an effort which somehow found its way past Porter at his near post. However it went in, nobody in amber and black was complaining, and Bridges were back on level terms.

The hosts continued to press for a winner, and debutant Jadyn Dundas should have put them ahead just minutes after coming off the bench. Arriving at the back post with the goal at his mercy, he was unable to get his feet sorted out in time to convert. What then followed was an end-to-end contest, with Sam Granville striking the crossbar for Cheshunt before Leighton and Velvick both saw efforts bravely blocked by visiting defenders.

This time, though, Bridges were not to be denied. Cheshunt failed to deal with the danger inside their own penalty area, and after Porter could only parry an initial deflected effort, the ball fell kindly into the path of Noel Leighton. The striker made no mistake from close range, sending Jubilee Field into celebration and, more importantly, putting Bridges 2-1 ahead.

The home side looked relatively comfortable heading towards the final whistle, but injury time brought one final scare. An almighty scramble inside the Bridges six-yard box threatened to produce a late Cheshunt equaliser, with the visitors seemingly doing everything they could to force the ball over the line. Somehow, the Bridges defence stood firm and managed to clear their lines before the referee finally blew for full-time.

There was an enormous sigh of relief around Jubilee Field as Three Bridges secured just their third league victory of the season. A hugely important result for Jamie Crellin's side, and one which could prove to be a turning point in their season.

If the great escape is to become a reality, Jubilee Field must now become a fortress, starting next Saturday afternoon when Wingate & Finchley visit for another crucial encounter.

#1930. Cherki magic helping Maresca to step out of Guardiola shadow

Rumours of Manchester City’s supposed demise without Pep Guardiola appear to be much exaggerated.

They swept past Crystal Palace at Selhurst Park with a style of play under new manager Enzo Maresca that was just as swashbuckling as under his predecessor, with Rayan Cherki playing the role of chief architect. The Frenchman’s two goals included a captivating mazy dribble, which will long be remembered by those who had the fortune to see it.

City created enough space for themselves through clever movement. With Cherki zigging one way and Phil Foden zagging the other, they created even more by dribbling past a mesmerised Palace back three that became a back five at times and still could not cope.

Erling Haaland also scored twice. Even with the creative and unpredictable talents of those behind in a four-man attacking City midfield, Haaland remains irreplaceable with his ability to convert chances.

However, this night belonged to Cherki. Guardiola chided him publicly after he set up a City goal with a “rabona” cross last season. The thrust of Guardiola’s comments were that Cherki was not Lionel Messi. Of course not, but he possesses a genius all of his own, which Maresca would surely be foolish to rein in.

The jaw-dropping splendour of Cherki’s first goal drew a collective intake of breath at Selhurst Park.

Collecting a Foden pass, he attacked the Palace area on a diagonal path, slaloming between Jaydee Canvot, Takehiro Tomiyasu and Chris Richards, before having the spatial awareness and technique to flick his left foot at the ball to send it rolling on a perpendicular trajectory past Dean Henderson.

"The man with the magic feet!"Rayan Cherki doubles Manchester City's lead with a STUNNING goal 😮‍💨 pic.twitter.com/9Zea5vFljv

An insight into Cherki’s mindset came after the match.

He said: “My performance is s---. In the first half, we didn’t find the space, I played bad. I need to show them that I want to play, I want to score. Next time I want to give the ball around more.”

Forget the words, Maresca cannot ignore the actions of a player he left on the bench against Bournemouth.

Sterner tests will come for City than against a Palace side missing key players who may or may not leave south London in the remaining days of the transfer window.

Whether Maresca will trust his forward players to express themselves as freely against their rivals for the Premier League title remains to be seen, but with Elliot Anderson providing a one-man shield behind them, City could not be stopped.

Maresca said: “For sure Rayan is happy tonight. His performance was very good and not just for his two goals. He has to press off the ball and he was in charge of [marking] Adam Wharton, so it was a complete game by him.”

Only for the first three minutes did Palace hint at a different outcome but, after shots from Eddie Nketiah and Daichi Kamada were diverted away for corners, City took control.

They took the lead in the 17th minute when the otherwise quiet Antoine Semenyo flighted a cross over the heads of everyone except the shorn locks of Haaland, whose determined header looped over Henderson and dropped in the far corner.

The only negative of Foden’s performance came in front of goal, with a ballooned shot and a mistimed header.

After Cherki’s solo masterpiece had made it 2-0, Yeremy Pino seized the next moment for his own with a stunning free-kick that flicked the crossbar, then the back of City keeper Gianluigi Donnarumma before finally dropping over the line.

"This is a good a free-kick as you're likely to see this season!" Yéremy Pino's stirke beats Donnarumma 🎯 pic.twitter.com/5uF4vzOXDp

Whatever hope that mustered was snatched away again when Cherki scored his second goal and the third goal of a breathless five minutes.

His shot at the end of a darting run flicked the ankle of Tomiyasu to send it just out of Henderson’s reach.

Rayan Cherki AGAIN! Manchester City have breathing room once again after another strike from the Frenchman 👏 pic.twitter.com/Tyw9whPS2r

Morocco teenager Ayyoub Bouaddi had little time to show why City have paid Lille £85.6m for him with a late entry as a substitute, but they didn’t need him on this occasion.

Foden then set off on a swerving run that set up Haaland to lash home his second goal of the game and make it 4-1.

Erling Haaland scores gets another! 🔥 pic.twitter.com/4mz2eF7wFF

The fear for Palace is that they cannot keep selling their best players and expecting to replicate the success on the pitch that has brought them three trophies in the past 15 months.

Leicester City offer a shuddering example of that. From Premier League champions to League One in 10 seasons.

Pierre Sage, the new Palace manager, will welcome the certainty that the closure of the transfer window will bring, particularly over the futures of forwards Ismaïla Sarr and Jean-Philippe Mateta, as well as wing-back Daniel Muñoz.

The one player he cannot afford to lose is Wharton, who matched the City midfield on his own at times in the first half.

Sage said: “I think the score is heavy. We stayed in the game for 65 minutes and created some chances. We know we are in for a tough season, but we have created a lot of opportunities in the first two games.

“I could speak about the transfer window, but I don’t want to find an excuse. We just have to be sure that in four days’ time, the team will be better than today.”

“It has been a short pre-season. Rayan [Cherki], five weeks ago was at the World Cup. Game by game, we will be back, just need a few games. We played well, it is a new manager but we have been playing together, with the addition of a few new players. We know what to do and have to trust the system.”

“We have to keep on playing together, find out where we are best and how to play. We have so many good players and we have to fit everyone in. He has to keep going because we know how good Phil is, it is about showing it week in week out. This is the right step forward for everyone. We have to build on this.”

"I'm just trying to play my football" 💪Elliot Anderson is excited about the future at Manchester City after his summer transfer 🔥 pic.twitter.com/huGv4Li3GZ

"Say what you actually mean!" 🤣Erling Haaland takes over Rayan Cherki's post-match interview! pic.twitter.com/adW6IU8DzQ

Nearly an instant impact from McAidoo as the 18-year-old drives through the Palace half and curls a shot from the edge of the box that goes just wide.

When Manchester City were making those substitutions, the Crystal Palace fans were making sure they let the officials know how long the Manchester City players were taking to get off.

There is going to be a debut for the Premier League’s most expensive teenager ever as Bouaddi comes on for Manchester City. McAidoo is also coming on, with Cherki and Anderson going off.

Mingueza eventually comes on but not after having to wait until the ball goes out of play again as Khalaili was adjudged to have taken too long to have got off the pitch. Safe to say the Palace fans are not too impressed with that new rule. It will probably be a pub question in the years ahead. That change does mean that Palace have used all five substitutions, which means Munoz will not come on. He is being linked with a reunion with Oliver Glasner at Nottingham Forest in the final days of this window.

Crystal Palace make another double change and it will be two debuts as Disasi and Mingueza come on.

Enzo Maresca turns to his bench for the first time tonight as Kovacic comes on.

Khalaili brings down Semenyo and is booked for that challenge.

Palace are going to make a double substitution as McNeil and Gozo replace Nketiah and Pino. 19-year-old Gozo is on for his Palace debut.

That was a chance for Palace. Guessand finds Pino, who drives into the Manchester City penalty area on the right. Pino has Nketiah at the far post but there is too much on the cross.

Guessand, back at Palace, is going to come on to replace Strand Larsen, who has been pretty quiet up top for the home side tonight.

Sometimes you feel blessed to witness an extraordinary moment of footballing genius. Selhurst Park has just seen two in the space of three minutes. Yeremy Pino’s free-kick which flicked off the back of Gianluigi Donnarumma was stunning, but even that could not truly compare to the slalom run of Rayan Cherki that drew a collective intake of breath from all those present. The Frenchman has just followed it with a scorching shot. It couldn’t compare with his first, though.

Three goals come in quick succession and Cherki restores Manchester City’s two-goal advantage with his second of the night. The Frenchman receives it on the turn from around 30 yards out and drives towards the Palace penalty area. He then shoots and a kind deflection off Richards takes it over Henderson’s diving effort and into the Palace net.

Rayan Cherki AGAIN! Manchester City have breathing room once again after another strike from the Frenchman 👏 pic.twitter.com/Tyw9whPS2r

Just as the hosts appeared to maybe out of this one, they get a goal back. Pino’s fantastic free-kick strikes the bar, hits Donnarumma on the back before going into the net off the post. That hit the frame of the goal twice and Palace have a crucial goal, minutes after going 2-0 down.

"This is a good a free-kick as you're likely to see this season!" Yéremy Pino's stirke beats Donnarumma 🎯 pic.twitter.com/5uF4vzOXDp

Anderson brings down Pino not far outside the Manchester City penalty area and is booked.

The next goal in this game felt crucial and the visitors have it. Foden drives towards the Palace penalty area before playing a pass forward into the path of Cherki. The Frenchman has numerous defenders around but he shows neat footwork to skip past a few, holds off Richards before slotting home with his left foot.

"The man with the magic feet!"Rayan Cherki doubles Manchester City's lead with a STUNNING goal 😮‍💨 pic.twitter.com/9Zea5vFljv

No-one has had fewer touches on the pitch tonight than Haaland up until this point but the Norwegian’s goal is the difference. His number of touches (14) is the joint fewest with his compatriot Strand Larsen.

That was a good chance for Nketiah. He plays the ball to the underlapping Mitchell, who from the byline cuts it back into the path of Nketiah. The former Arsenal man should so so much better with his opportunity from the edge of the six-yard box but fires a long way wide.

Semenyo wins Manchester City an early corner in this second half off Canvot. Anderson’s delivery beyond the back post picks out O’Reilly, who in space heads back across goal but Pino heads away.

We are back under way at Selhurst Park, with Manchester City carrying a 1-0 lead into this second half. As the players emerged from the tunnels for the second half, the DJ at Selhurst Park paid tribute to the late Dolly Parton and Kenny Rogers by playing Islands in the Stream. Nice touch! Get your favourite Dolly and Kenny tunes in the comments section at the bottom of the blog.

Possession: Crystal Palace 33%-67% Manchester CityShots: 7-11Shots on target: 1-6Corners: 2-2Touches in the opposition box: 10-18

The stats are certainly in Manchester City’s favour and they will feel they probably should have more than the one goal.

Cherki has a late chance for Manchester City but his shot is well saved by Henderson down to his right.

The first half at Selhurst Park is then brought to an end and Manchester City lead 1-0 at the break thanks to Haaland’s header.

There will be just one added minute at the end of this first half.

Palace started off with a nominal back three. That has become a back five far too often for Pierre Sage’s liking at times in this first half, yet still City are playing through them almost at will. The Palace fans whose deafening support accompanied Palace shots in the opening minutes are reduced to cheering battling midfield runs that win a free-kick now.

Pino delivers a free-kick into the Manchester City box and Richards gets to it first. It comes off his shoulder and rolls into the arms of Donnarumma.

Semenyo’s shot from the left side of the box takes a deflection off Richards, forcing Henderson into a decent save.

Palace now miss a big opportunity and should be on level terms. Wharton, who has probably been the best player on the pitch tonight, whips in a cross from the right and picks out Mitchell, who has a free header from eight yards out but somehow misses the target.

Strand Larsen comes close with a header from a Pino cross but he would have been offside anyway.

The first booking of the night goes the way of the visitors. Wharton drives forward into the Manchester City half and is cynically brought down by Cherki, who looked perplexed when the yellow card was shown but it was an obvious booking.

Foden wastes his second big chance of this first half. Manchester City break through O’Reilly, who carries it down the right. He waits for Cherki to make the overlapping run before passing to the Frenchman. Cherki’s cross picks out Foden inside the six-yard box and the latter should score but he gets a simple header all wrong.

Well, that was easy. So easy in fact – perfect Semenyo cross, perfect Haaland header - that it hushed Selhurst Park as the ball looped over Dean Henderson. Even the roar from the enclave of City fans took a moment to fill the south London air. You wouldn’t say that all the pre-match optimism among Palace fans has been punctured, but the home side need a moment if they aren’t to sink without trace to a City side bossing possession and territory now.

That is a huge miss from Foden. Anderson picks out his compatriot in acres of space on the right side of the box, with no Palace defender within five yards of him, but Foden blazes over the bar when he should have put Manchester City 2-0 up.

King Harald V of Norway has died in the last few days and over the last few hours two Norwegian cyclists claimed a one-two at the Vuelta a Espana and now Haaland has a goal.

He has barely touched the ball thus far but he puts the visitors ahead just past the quarter-of-an-hour mark. Semenyo is afforded too much space on the left just outside the penalty area and clips in a cross towards the far post. Haaland gets up highest, above Richards, and guides a superb header over Henderson into the Palace net.

Erling Haaland gets off the mark for the new Premier League season! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/5ZjQUVk6Zl

The England boss is in attendance tonight, perhaps keeping a close eye on that midfield battle between Anderson and Wharton.

Palace flirt with danger inside their own penalty area. After Haaland’s flick, Kamada should just belt the ball away but instead inexplicably leaves it. Henderson manages to mop up just as Foden was eyeing up the chance.

There is a mad scramble inside the Palace box but somehow the hosts escape without conceding. Initially, Anderson’s shot from range is saved by Henderson but Manchester City keep it alive in the penalty area. Palace frantically attempt to clear their lines and eventually they do after Haaland came close.

Quite a lot of the focus tonight will be on two English midfielders; one who has got a big-money move this summer and the other thus far has not. Anderson is directly up against Wharton and so far it is the latter who is winning the early battles, including dispossessing Anderson in midfield.

The first chance of the game goes the way of the hosts. It stems from a quite sensational first-time pass from Wharton from inside his own half into the left channel to pick out the run of Nketiah, whose shot from the left side of the box takes a deflection off Dias and is saved by Donnarumma.

Manchester City initially clear the corner but Palace keep it alive. Kamada’s shot from just inside the box appeared to be on target but it is headed over for another corner, which is easily caught by Donnarumma.

We are under way at Selhurst Park. Will Pierre Sage earn his first win as Palace boss or can Enzo Maresca and City make it two wins from two?

Both sides emerge from the tunnel in the corner of Selhurst Park to the customary sound of Glad All Over and we are moments away from kick-off in south London. Here is a reminder of how the two sides line up this evening:

Crystal Palace: Henderson, Khalaili, Canvot, Richards, Tomiyasu, Mitchell, Wharton, Kamada, Pino, Strand Larsen, Nketiah.Substitutes: Benitez, Munoz, Disasi, Mingueza, Hughes, Lerma, Gozo, McNeil, Guessand.

Manchester City: Donnarumma, Khusanov, Dias, Gvardiol, O’Reilly, Anderson, Guehi, Cherki, Foden Semenyo, Haaland.Substitutes: Rulli, Kovacic, Ait-Nouri, Reis, Echeverri, Bouaddi, McAidoo, Braithwaite, Lewis.

Yes! It may have been fleeting but the boy in the Palace tracksuit top had his moment after all with Erling Haaland as City waited in line to enter the Selhurst Park pitch. And having done so, he fairly skipped up the steps back with his dad back to their seats. Whether the boy’s second wish of the evening, for a Palace victory, will come true is another question altogether.

The young Palace fan is still waiting for Haaland. Another determined walk back to the dressing room. It isn’t a simple task to attract an opposition player’s attention when you are leaning over a barrier a few feet higher than him – and in the home end. Haaland and his teammates have the look of a team that knows it must perform tonight to ease the concerns that they are a team in transition. The City fans will not entertain such thoughts, either.

Crystal Palace looked set to sign Club Brugge defender Joel Ordonez but that deal could be in doubt as there may be some problems with his medical. We await to see further updates on that situation.

“He is a genius. Make no mistake. Managers now want structure, they do not like players who are a bit loose out of possession. But I go to football matches to watch people like him play.

“That is what makes me smile. I do not like watching players pass it sideways, that is not why I go to football. I go to watch geniuses do their work. Some managers will not appreciate it. But last week he got his manager out of a hole because without him they would not have won that game.”

"He's irreplaceable" 💥Jamie Redknapp and Clinton Morrison sing the praises of Crystal Palace's Adam Wharton 🤝 pic.twitter.com/ZOpcZcItHY

Jack Grealish is not in the Manchester City squad tonight amid links with the likes of Everton and Sunderland. Will he still be at the club beyond the deadline? It would appear not.

Both Ismaila Sarr and Jean-Philippe Mateta are out of the Crystal Palace squad tonight with injury but could they be on the move before the window slams shut? Sarr has been linked with Galatasaray and Liverpool whilst the situation is complicated with Mateta as he claims the final year of his contract is void. How do those two situations resolve themselves? Daniel Munoz has been linked with a move to Nottingham Forest but is on the bench for Palace this evening.

An unfulfilled wish so far for a young Palace fan holding up a child’s red Norway shirt with ‘Haaland’ emblazoned on it. Having waited patiently for the City players to emerge for their warm-up and being held by his dad as he leant over the stone wall to attract Haaland’s attention, he was left disappointed because the City striker was simply not looking as he and his teammates jogged past. Will the boy, who has on a Palace tracksuit top, get a photo with his hero when the striker returns to the Portakabin that hosts the away dressing room prior to kick-off? Stay tuned.

"The results will certainly come" ✅Dean Henderson urges patience as Crystal Palace go through a transitional period under new manager Pierre Sage 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/1pJjRPeKko

"On the ball I think he's very good, off the ball he's strong" Enzo Maresca explains why he played Marc Guéhi in midfield in Manchester City's opening game against Bournemouth 🤔 pic.twitter.com/h4N1e1L8bf

"At home anything is possible" 💪Pierre Sage previews his sides clash with Manchester City at Selhurst Park 🔥 pic.twitter.com/oPJnZJVB6B

Crystal Palace: Henderson, Khalaili, Canvot, Richards, Tomiyasu, Mitchell, Wharton, Kamada, Pino, Strand Larsen, Nketiah.Substitutes: Benitez, Munoz, Disasi, Mingueza, Hughes, Lerma, Gozo, McNeil, Guessand.

There looks set to be a debut for the Premier League’s most expensive teenager off the visitors’ bench in the form of Ayyoub Bouaddi. There is no Jack Grealish in their squad as his future is up in the air.

Manchester City: Donnarumma, Khusanov, Dias, Gvardiol, O’Reilly, Anderson, Guehi, Cherki, Foden Semenyo, Haaland.Substitutes: Rulli, Kovacic, Ait-Nouri, Reis, Echeverri, Bouaddi, McAidoo, Braithwaite, Lewis.

Was it really just a year ago when Crystal Palace fans flooded down the Holmesdale Road with not a care in the world having just won the Community Shield to add to their FA Cup triumph over tonight’s opponents Manchester City? Well, they are marching along the Holmesdale Road in the same numbers again this evening, bedecked in red and blue as always, yet there is uncertainty and worry in the air and on their faces. Will the player exodus continue? What should they make of new manager Pierre Sage? Will the good times fade from view as quickly as they did for Leicester City or can Sage build a new side to match the one which, under Oliver Glasner, added the Conference League to their list of trophies three months ago?

“We struggled to get into the game and win the battles,” a disappointed Carlo Ancelotti lamented.

At the World Cup, an industrious 18-year-old showed maturity beyond his years to dominate the midfield against Ancelotti’s Brazil on his competitive international debut, earning Morocco a draw. That was, in fact, the second time an Ancelotti side had been undone by precocious teenager Ayyoub Bouaddi.

Ancelotti’s remarks about losing the midfield battle are from after a Champions League match in October 2024, when Lille shocked Real Madrid to end their 36-game unbeaten run. Bouaddi was at the heart of both statement results for his club and country.

Tonight:Crystal Palace vs Manchester City

Saturday:Liverpool vs Nottingham ForestBournemouth vs EvertonCoventry vs Hull CityTottenham vs Newcastle

Sunday:Chelsea vs BrightonLeeds vs BrentfordSunderland vs FulhamManchester United vs Ipswich

Tonight's team to face Crystal Palace! ​​💪🩵XI | Donnarumma, Khusanov, Dias (C), Gvardiol, O'Reilly, Anderson, Guéhi, Foden, Cherki, Semenyo, HaalandSUBS | Rulli, Kovačić, Aït-Nouri, Reis, Echeverri, Bouaddi, McAidoo, Braithwaite, Lewis🤝 @etihad pic.twitter.com/qNgJPXKDM7

The second weekend of the Premier League season kicks off under the lights in South London as Crystal Palace host Manchester City at Selhurst Park. Manchester City won both fixtures 3-0 last season and they are in fact unbeaten in their last 11 Premier league away games against Crystal Palace, who have won just two of the 22 top flight meetings.

Crystal Palace experienced defeat on the opening weekend, falling to a 2-0 loss at Everton last Saturday, meaning the Pierre Sage era started with a defeat. Tonight is Sage’s first home game in charge of the club.

“I think it will be a wonderful moment, but I prefer to have a wonderful moment with good news at the end of the game,” Sage said. “That is why I do not think about me in this situation. The most important thing is the team and the result for sure, because we prepare all the week for that, to make them [the fans] happy. They will be happy to see us, but I think they would prefer to see us win. I will give my life to make them happy. I cannot do more. When you are in this stadium [Selhurst Park], you feel the history. You feel that there is something heavy weighing on you. It is a great responsibility that I have been entrusted with. We cannot wait to see this stadium in action.”

Sage has confirmed that Ismaila Sarr, who has been linked with a move away from the club this summer, and Chadi Riad will miss out tonight due to injury, as will striker Jean-Philippe Mateta. Palace have confirmed the addition of Axel Disasi on loan from Chelsea and the French defender could be involved tonight.

Manchester City appeared to be heading towards defeat in Enzo Maresca’s first league game in charge of the club last weekend. They were 1-0 down at home against Bournemouth in the closing stages before goals from Marc Guehi and Josko Gvardiol gave them a come-from-behind win.

It has been a busy week in the transfer window for Manchester City. Both Savio (formerly Savinho) and Omar Marmoush have left for Tottenham, joining a long list of departures from the Etihad this summer. Moroccan midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi has arrived in an £85m deal from Lille and has become the most expensive teenager in Premier League history. Maresca has confirmed that 18-year-old Bouaddi is ready to start.

“He [Bouaddi] is ready,” Maresca said. “He was working with his former club so he is fit. We will see how long he needs in terms of adaptation but he is ready to go. He is quite calm. He does not look 18, he already looks older, which is important. But in this case, we need to go slowly because he is very young, he has come from a different country so there is no rush for him. He is going to help us now and in the future. He is very mature for being 18.”

Team news from Selhurst Park to follow shortly.
